description: A capital allocation director must authorize the company's minority investment in a payments-technology company and finalize the purchase price, funding tranches, governance rights, and closing controls, with input from legal, treasury, and strategic partnerships.

shared_context.S1: The company is considering purchasing a 30% interest in LedgerSpring, a payments-technology company, for a proposed total purchase price of $8,000,000.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding decision on the investment and its final conditions.
shared_context.S3: LedgerSpring has supplied two years of audited revenue statements and is seeking a signed investment commitment this month.
shared_context.S4: Under the capital-allocation process, Elena conducts a round-robin review with legal, treasury, and strategic partnerships before signing an investment decision.

PF1.text: Jonah found in the related-party review completed this morning that LedgerSpring's chair also owns a small supplier of the company's current payment terminals. The related-party policy therefore requires an independent valuation before signing and an audit-committee approval record before closing; Jonah has not yet added this finding to the investment file.

PF2.text: Mira's cash forecast, confirmed this morning after a debt-service update, shows that only $3,000,000 can be funded at signing while preserving the approved operating reserve. The remaining $5,000,000 can be funded exactly 90 days after signing; she has not yet circulated the updated forecast.

PF3.text: Tariq's term sheet call with LedgerSpring last week confirmed that the seller will accept a board-observer seat for the company, but will not grant a veto over LedgerSpring's regulated payment activities. Tariq recorded the agreed governance terms in his desk notes but has not put them into the draft investment approval.

acceptance_conditions: The investment must be approved at a total purchase price of exactly $8,000,000.
Exactly $3,000,000 must be funded at signing and exactly $5,000,000 must be funded 90 days later.
An independent valuation and audit-committee approval record must be required before closing.
The company must receive a board-observer right and must not receive a veto over LedgerSpring's regulated payment activities.
The settlement must include commitments for the independent valuation, the audit-committee approval record, and the two funding tranches.

content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'independent_valuation' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'audit_committee_approval' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The clean audited statements alone do not require special closing controls; PF1 changes independent_valuation_required and audit_committee_approval_required from false to true and adds both required approval commitments.

The proposed $8,000,000 price does not specify timing of funding; PF2 changes funding_at_signing_usd to exactly 3,000,000 and funding_after_90_days_usd to exactly 5,000,000 and requires the funding-tranche commitment.
The shared proposal says nothing about investor governance; PF3 changes board_observer_right to true while setting regulated_activity_veto to false.
